cases.why: A continuation-only line carrying TWO underscores. A continuation must be the last thing on its line - the corpus already has `_ 'comment` and `_z` after one, both illegal - so a second underscore should be no different. Raised because the grammar's new continuation-absorbing NEWLINE accepts it and nothing had asked. Predicting illegal.

The indented continuation-only line is measured legal with SPACES; this asks whether the required whitespace is spaces specifically or a whitespace run. Every other separator in this grammar turned out to be a run, and each time the narrow reading was the bug - so the prediction is legal, and getting it wrong either way is worth knowing.

Text after the underscore on an otherwise-empty continuation line. The control for the two-underscore case: if both are illegal the rule is simply 'nothing may follow', and if they differ the underscore is being treated as something other than trailing junk.

A continuation inside an empty argument list. Included because the new NEWLINE only absorbs a continuation line that follows a NEWLINE, and this one follows an open parenthesis - a position where the old hidden LINE_CONTINUATION is still the only thing that can match. If the two mechanisms have a seam, this is where it shows.
